name: Kopere Dashboard
description: A modular administrative workspace for Moodle that unifies Kopere tools, permissions, KPIs, audit trails and institutional workflows behind one interface.
description_html:
Administrative workspaceKopere foundation

Kopere Dashboard

Give administrative teams one operational workspace instead of sending them through dozens of unrelated Moodle administration screens.

The dashboard provides the shared navigation, layout, permissions, indicators and audit layer used by internal modules and by several independent plugins in the Kopere family.

One workspace, different roles
  • Academic and registrar routines.
  • Course and user lookup.
  • Documents, contracts and requests.
  • Reporting and operational indicators.
  • Backup, diagnostics and administrative tools.
  • Separate permissions for modules and sensitive actions.
Modular architecture
Features can live as internal dashboard modules or independent local_kopere_* plugins while still appearing in the same navigation and permission model.
Role-oriented access
Registrar, finance, coordination, support and administrators can receive only the tools relevant to their work instead of inheriting broad access to the whole administration tree.
Audit trail
Important actions can record who performed them, when they happened, which module was involved and which record was affected.
A foundation for the Kopere ecosystem

The dashboard is useful on its own, but its larger role is architectural: it gives other Kopere plugins a consistent administrative shell, shared visual language and common permission surface so each new tool does not need to invent another back office.

How it fits real Moodle workflows

The operational value of Kopere Dashboard appears when an institution needs a single entry point for several independent administrative routines. Course and user lookup, institutional indicators, management modules and permission-controlled tools can share one navigation model rather than being scattered across separate custom pages. Administrators should assign access according to job responsibilities and audit sensitive operations, while extensions can build on the shared workspace without becoming part of the Moodle core. The dashboard is an integration surface, not a substitute for the underlying permissions of each installed module.

name: Boost Magnific
description: A highly customizable Boost-based Moodle theme focused on cleaner course presentation, responsive layouts and institution-level visual branding.
description_html:
Boost-based themeMoodle 4.4+

Boost Magnific

Refresh Moodle's visual presentation while retaining the familiar Boost-based structure administrators and course teams already know.

Boost Magnific focuses on a cleaner interface, responsive behavior and configurable institutional branding rather than replacing Moodle's learning model with a separate front end.

Presentation controls
  • Responsive layouts for desktop and mobile use.
  • Configurable colors, logos and visual identity.
  • Refined course and navigation presentation.
  • Theme-level adjustments for activity and interface styling.
Institutional branding
Adapt Moodle's colors and identity without asking course authors to recreate branding inside each course.
Course readability
Theme styling gives course content and navigation a more deliberate visual hierarchy while preserving Moodle functionality.
Responsive foundation
The theme is intended to keep the experience consistent across common desktop, tablet and mobile viewport sizes.
Features in practice

Boost Magnific is intended for institutions that want to shape a consistent Moodle appearance while retaining familiar course editing and navigation. Administrators can combine the theme's presentation and branding choices instead of applying local CSS patches on individual pages. In practice, the most important review is not the theme's landing page alone: check a real course with long titles, activities, blocks and responsive navigation. Teachers should be able to keep working with standard Moodle resources while learners see the institutional identity across screens. A visual configuration is not a replacement for accessibility review, and a theme does not alter grading, enrolment or completion rules.

name: Degrade Theme
description: A responsive Moodle theme with a minimalist visual direction, configurable colors and branding, and a cleaner presentation of standard Moodle pages.
description_html:
Responsive themeMoodle 4.4+

Degrade

Give standard Moodle pages a softer, more minimalist visual identity while keeping courses and administration recognizably Moodle.

Degrade is aimed at sites that want a polished institutional theme with straightforward branding controls rather than a radically different application experience.

Theme focus
  • Responsive presentation across common devices.
  • Configurable colors and logos.
  • Cleaner typography and page spacing.
  • Visual adjustments for standard Moodle interfaces.
Minimal visual direction
The theme emphasizes clarity and spacing instead of filling pages with additional decorative interface layers.
Brand controls
Administrators can adapt the visual identity to better match the institution without editing every course individually.
Familiar Moodle behavior
The theme changes presentation while keeping the underlying Moodle workflows and page concepts intact.
Features in practice

Degrade offers a minimalist, responsive visual treatment for standard Moodle pages. Its design uses softer colors and readable typography to reduce unnecessary interface clutter, while the underlying Moodle course structure remains familiar. Administrators can select the theme and check representative course pages, editing controls, dashboards and common activity screens at mobile and desktop widths. This is useful for institutions that need a consistent public-facing appearance without rebuilding their learning activities. Contrast, keyboard behavior and custom blocks should still be tested against real content; updating the presentation does not automatically make every installed extension accessible.

name: Mod Super Video
description: Add tracked video activities with resume, viewing maps, reports and configurable playback for YouTube, Vimeo, Google Drive and supported integrations.
description_html:
Tracked video activityResume and viewing map

Super Video

Turn a hosted video into a Moodle activity that remembers where the learner stopped and records which parts of the timeline were actually watched.

Super Video supports common hosted-video sources including YouTube, Vimeo and Google Drive, while keeping playback, learner progress and reporting inside the course activity.

What teachers get
  • Responsive video playback inside Moodle.
  • Automatic resume from the learner's last position.
  • A viewing map showing consumed timeline segments.
  • Reports for learner views and watched areas.
  • Site-wide defaults that teachers can override per activity.
Resume playback
Learners can return to the activity without manually searching for the point where they stopped.
Viewing map
Progress is based on watched portions of the video rather than assuming that reaching the end means every segment was consumed.
Operational reports
Teachers can inspect views and viewing-map information when they need evidence of how learners consumed the activity.
Designed as an activity, not a generic embed. The video participates in the course structure and can carry its own activity settings and reporting workflow.
How it fits real Moodle workflows

SuperVideo allows a teacher to add media as an activity rather than embedding an unmanaged link in arbitrary course HTML. Activity settings can control the presentation and tracking features used by that lesson, while site-level configuration provides consistency across courses. Teachers should test the chosen provider and viewing experience with realistic learner devices and network conditions. A successfully opened player is not automatically evidence of meaningful video consumption, so progress and completion decisions should follow the functionality actually supported by the configured source.

name: GeniAI
description: Artificial intelligence features that support content creation and learning.
description_html:
AI-assisted learningMoodle course context

GeniAI

Add a contextual virtual assistant to Moodle courses and support teachers with interactive H5P content creation and AI usage reporting.

GeniAI brings student questions and teacher content-development tasks closer to the courses they relate to, without requiring learners to search for a separate assistant outside Moodle.

Main capabilities
  • A chat assistant available from course pages.
  • Course-related answers informed by the current course and user language.
  • AI-assisted creation and management of supported H5P materials.
  • Usage reports with model, token and date information.
  • CSV export for administrative analysis.
A contextual assistant for learners

When enabled, a chat control can appear on course pages. The assistant receives relevant Moodle context, such as course name, language and available modules, and is instructed to answer questions in the context of the student's course. Learners can continue a conversation or clear its history when needed.

The assistant is designed for guidance and explanations, but its responses can still be incorrect or incomplete. Teachers remain responsible for the learning material and for decisions that require reliable academic evidence.

Create and manage interactive H5P content

Teachers and authorized administrators can use the supported H5P workflow to provide a topic or source material, generate interactive content, review it and send it to Moodle's Content Bank. Supported content types depend on the installed integration and implementation; formats such as glossaries, flashcards and quizzes are among the project's intended use cases.

AI-produced activities should be inspected and edited before publication. Parts of the generation workflow may involve an external support service, so institutions should review data handling and privacy rules before production use.

Usage visibility and operational boundaries

Administrative reporting can show the model used, input and output token counts, request dates and related operational metadata, with CSV export for further analysis. These records help administrators monitor usage and approximate API consumption rather than leaving costs unexplained.

Configure API access and available models according to the current provider requirements; availability and pricing can change. Avoid unnecessary personal data in prompts, and maintain human oversight of generated responses and instructional materials.

name: Beautiful Certificate
description: Create visually polished Moodle certificates from reusable templates, dynamic learner and course data, institutional branding and PDF output.
description_html:
Certificate activityPDF output

Beautiful Certificate

Issue certificates that look like finished institutional documents instead of treating certification as a plain text export.

Teachers can start from reusable certificate designs and combine visual customization with dynamic Moodle information such as learner, course, enrolment and teacher data.

Built for reusable designs
  • Multiple ready-to-use certificate styles.
  • Custom text, colors, logos and visual identity.
  • Dynamic learner and course information.
  • Teacher, enrolment and profile data options.
  • Certificate generation as PDF.
Template library
Start from different visual styles rather than designing every certificate from a blank page.
Dynamic data
Personalize issued certificates with Moodle data so the same design can be reused across learners and courses.
Institutional presentation
Use logos, colors and layout choices to make the certificate reflect the identity of the institution or course.
How it fits real Moodle workflows

Beautiful Certificate focuses on the full certificate workflow: designing a reusable layout, inserting learner and course information, applying institutional visual identity and generating a PDF for the eligible participant. Teachers and administrators can avoid hand-editing an image or document for each learner, while templates keep repeated certificates visually consistent. The certificate should use trusted dynamic values from Moodle instead of requiring recipients to type their own credentials. Institutions should review issuance conditions, template accuracy and how generated documents are distributed before using certificates for formal recognition.

name: Alternative File System
description: Move Moodle's filedir to AWS S3 or DigitalOcean Spaces and serve files through remote object storage for scalable, shared infrastructure.
description_html:
Object storageMoodle filedir

Alternative File System

Move moodledata/filedir away from one server disk and let Moodle read and serve files through remote object storage.

The plugin currently supports AWS S3 and DigitalOcean Spaces and is designed for environments where file growth, multiple application nodes or storage maintenance make a local-only filedir increasingly painful.

Supported storage
  • AWS S3.
  • DigitalOcean Spaces.
  • S3-compatible behavior may depend on the endpoint and should be validated before production use.
  • CDN delivery can be combined with the storage architecture when the selected provider and deployment support it.
Shared file storage
Object storage provides a common file location for clustered or multi-node Moodle deployments instead of binding filedir to one application server.
Controlled migration
Existing local filedir content can be transferred to the configured remote storage before the alternative file-system class becomes the active source.
tool_objectfs transition
A migration path can detect an existing tool_objectfs setup, reuse relevant settings and validate the new destination before switching the file-system class.
Why move filedir at all?

On larger sites, local filedir eventually becomes an infrastructure problem: disks grow, backups get heavier, horizontal scaling needs shared storage and server replacement becomes entangled with a large content volume.

Object storage does not magically make every request faster, but it separates application compute from file capacity and gives operations a storage layer that can scale, replicate and be managed independently.

Activation is explicit: after the remote destination is prepared, Moodle must be configured to use \local_alternative_file_system\external_file_system as its alternative file-system class in config.php.

name: Kopere APP Mobile
description: Mobile integration for Moodle with offline-aware content delivery, optimized file access and native app workflows.
description_html:
Mobile integrationOffline-aware

Kopere APP Mobile

Keep Moodle course content usable when connectivity is slow, intermittent or temporarily unavailable, without turning the LMS into a separate mobile backend.

The plugin exposes Moodle-side services and file delivery behavior used by the dedicated app, including offline-friendly handling for supported resources and repository files.

Designed for real connectivity constraints
  • Supported resources can be cached or downloaded for later access.
  • External repository files can be served instead of redirected when offline delivery is requested.
  • Course and progress data continue to use Moodle APIs and permissions.
  • No Moodle core modification is required.
Course content
Supports offline-aware delivery for common resources such as folders, pages, files, URLs, pictures and integrated modules.
File optimization
Lets the app request a file representation suitable for mobile and offline consumption instead of depending on a live redirect.
Moodle-native access
Authentication, permissions and course data remain in Moodle rather than being duplicated in a parallel platform.
Offline availability depends on the resource or activity involved. Content that requires live server state may still need an internet connection.
How it fits real Moodle workflows

Kopere APP Mobile provides the integration surface for a branded mobile Moodle experience. Administrators should think about the application and the Moodle site as one deployment: the URL, authentication, available course content and mobile presentation must work together for learners. The value is not only a custom icon or splash screen, but providing a predictable route back to enrolled courses and institutional services. Institutions should test the experience with real devices, varying network conditions and the same access restrictions enforced by the web platform.

name: Copy and Paste Modules
description: Copy and paste activities and resources between courses with just a few clicks.
description_html:
Copy and Paste Modules

Copy one or more course activities and resources, move to another course or section, and paste them without rebuilding the content manually.

A persistent course clipboard

Teachers can copy an individual activity or use Moodle's bulk selection to place several items on the clipboard. The clipboard remains available while navigating to another course, so the destination does not need to be open at the same time as the source.

When pasting, the teacher chooses the destination section and the exact insertion position instead of being limited to a generic paste-at-the-end action.

Reuse the same selection more than once

A successful paste does not automatically clear the clipboard. The same copied activities can therefore be reused in multiple courses or sections without returning to the original course for every copy. A separate clear action is available when the clipboard is no longer needed.

Permission-aware copying

Copy, paste and clear operations are protected by the current Moodle session, and the plugin revalidates permissions for both the source and destination when content is pasted. The interface is shown only to users allowed to manage the copy workflow in the course.

Failures do not destroy the clipboard

If an item cannot be restored at the destination, the failure is reported for that activity while the clipboard remains available. This makes multi-item copying more practical because one failed item does not force the teacher to repeat the whole selection process.

name: Boost Dark
description: Add a persistent light/dark mode toggle to Boost and compatible child themes while storing each user's visual preference in Moodle.
description_html:
Dark modeBoost-compatible

Boost Dark

Add a user-controlled dark-mode switch to Boost and compatible child themes without replacing the active theme.

The selected mode is stored in Moodle user preferences so learners and staff can keep their preferred presentation when they return.

Lightweight behavior
  • Adds a light/dark toggle to the theme interface.
  • Persists the user's choice through Moodle preferences.
  • Does not require replacing Boost with a dedicated dark theme.
  • Has been tested with several Boost-derived community themes.
Theme compatibility can vary. Boost-derived themes can override substantial CSS, so visual testing remains important before enabling dark mode site-wide.
Features in practice

Boost Dark gives Moodle users a visible way to select a dark appearance in Boost and compatible child themes, with the selection retained as a Moodle preference. Users returning from another browser can keep the same preference without configuring each course separately. The plugin is especially relevant to Moodle releases where the chosen Boost theme does not already provide a native colour-mode control. Moodle 5.3 introduced native light, dark and automatic colour modes; when that native implementation is configured, Boost Dark steps aside rather than competing with it. It is an interface preference, not a separate course theme or a change to activity behavior.

How it fits real Moodle workflows

The important deployment distinction is between sites that need a supplementary colour-mode switch and installations where native Boost already provides the desired light, dark and automatic choices. Before enabling the plugin, administrators should inspect the Moodle theme settings and make sure the resulting header does not present duplicate controls. The goal is a predictable preference for each user, not a site-wide CSS override that forces dark mode on everyone.

name: Kopere BI
description: More than 100 Moodle reports and dashboards covering learning, access, courses, users, assessments, activities, enrolments and operational analytics.
description_html:
Business intelligence100+ reports

Kopere BI

Turn Moodle's operational data into dashboards people can use without starting every management question with a custom SQL query.

Kopere BI combines ready-to-use reports with charts, interactive tables, information cards, maps and custom Mustache presentations for administrators, coordinators, managers and educators.

Coverage across Moodle
  • Students, users and instructors.
  • Courses, content and enrolments.
  • Access, login and activity indicators.
  • Grades, assessments and completion.
  • Quiz, forum, SCORM, assignment and feedback activity.
  • Competencies, badges and learning plans.
  • Revenue and other institutional indicators where data is available.
Visual dashboards
Use ApexCharts, KPI cards and custom layouts to make trends and distributions visible without exporting everything first.
Operational tables
Large result sets can use searchable, sortable and paginated DataTables with export options according to the report implementation.
Custom presentation
Reports are not limited to one table format; Mustache output can present the same data as cards, summaries, lists or specialized management views.
Learning analytics without opening the event log on every page

The learning-analytics area includes operational dashboards such as overview indicators, learner attention queues, course health, Student 360, progress-versus-grade analysis and learning momentum.

These dashboards can read compact snapshot tables rebuilt by scheduled tasks instead of repeatedly aggregating the full standard log when a user opens a page, which is the difference between an analytics screen and a denial-of-service attack wearing a nice chart.

Kopere Dashboard foundation: the current plugin depends on local_kopere_dashboard, which provides the shared administrative workspace used by Kopere BI.

name: Star Rating
description: Add a simple 1-to-5 star course rating block and show learners the current average rating directly inside Moodle.
description_html:
Course feedback1 to 5 stars

Star Rating

Give learners a low-friction way to rate a course without turning a quick sentiment signal into a full survey.

Users choose a score from one to five stars and the block displays the aggregated average in the course interface.

Useful when you need
  • A fast course-level satisfaction signal.
  • A visible average rating.
  • A lightweight complement to richer questionnaires and feedback activities.
Scope: this is intentionally a lightweight rating signal. Use Moodle Feedback or Questionnaire when you need multiple questions, anonymous surveys or richer qualitative feedback.
Features in practice

Star Rating provides a compact five-star feedback mechanism in a Moodle block. Teachers can place it in a supported course context and invite participants to select a rating without completing a separate survey. The block also displays an aggregated average, allowing visitors to see the overall rating at a glance. It is most useful as a quick pulse, while a dedicated Moodle feedback activity remains preferable when detailed comments or structured questionnaires are required. A mean star value is not an evaluation of teaching effectiveness or student achievement; it summarizes only the ratings that people chose to submit.

How it fits real Moodle workflows

In a course with many participants, a visible aggregate can provide a low-effort indication of perceived quality, but it is worth considering who is allowed to rate and how representative the responses are. For deeper evaluation, pair the block with comments or Moodle Feedback rather than expecting a five-star average to explain why people are satisfied or dissatisfied. The plugin keeps the interface deliberately small.

name: User Field DB
description: Create Moodle user profile fields whose selectable values come from database tables, keeping institutional data lists consistent and reusable.
description_html:
User profile fieldDatabase-backed options

User Field DB

Use controlled database-backed lists for profile information that should not be entered as free text.

Administrators define the source table, key/value columns and optional filtering so users can select standardized values such as department, branch or cost center.

Why it helps
  • Reduces spelling and naming inconsistencies.
  • Keeps selectable options centrally maintained.
  • Creates structured profile data that can be reused by reporting tools such as Kopere BI.
Features in practice

User Field DB makes institutional reference tables available as controlled choices in Moodle user profile fields. An administrator selects the source table, the identifier and display columns and any supported filters, then publishes a field that users can fill by selecting an approved option. This is useful for departments, organizational units, branches or cost centers where multiple spellings would make later reports inconsistent. The options can follow updates to the database reference list, reducing repeated manual profile administration. This plugin creates a field type, not an authoritative data source: administrators remain responsible for the underlying table, values and access permissions.

How it fits real Moodle workflows

For reporting integrations, choose a stable identifier column and a readable label column, because administrators may rename departments while reports still need consistent keys. Before exposing a large table as profile choices, verify the size and filtering of the list as well as who maintains the source records. The strength of a database-backed field is reusable reference data; the operational risk is depending on a poorly governed table.

name: Moodle Course Backup
description: Automate Moodle course backups to FTP, restore archived courses and migrate backup sets between Moodle installations through a token-based transfer workflow.
description_html:
Course backupRestore and migration

Moodle Course Backup

Move course backups out of the day-to-day Moodle interface, organize them remotely and make restoration a controlled operational workflow instead of a hunt for old .mbz files.

The plugin automates course backups to FTP, organizes archives by course category and provides restoration tools for both stored backups and transfers from another Moodle installation.

Backup lifecycle
  1. Create the Moodle course backup.
  2. Transfer it to the configured FTP destination.
  3. Organize archives by course category.
  4. Browse stored backups from the restore interface.
  5. Queue restoration through Moodle tasks.
Remote archive
Keep course backup files on the configured FTP server instead of relying only on the Moodle application server's local disk.
Restore interface
Select backups from the stored archive and send restoration work to the normal Moodle processing flow.
Moodle-to-Moodle transfer
A new Moodle can connect to the previous installation using its wwwroot, an optional old server IP and a temporary transfer token, then list and queue selected remote backups.
Useful during server and platform migrations

The token-based transfer API means a migration does not have to begin by manually copying every backup file. The destination can discover the available remote backups, preserve source course/category context and queue the selected restores for CRON processing.

How it fits real Moodle workflows

A backup service becomes useful only when restoring the result is part of the plan. Moodle Course Backup automates archive creation and transfer, with workflows for recovering courses and moving backup sets between installations. Administrators should review schedules, remote storage credentials, retention rules and the permissions required for a restore, rather than equating an uploaded archive with disaster recovery. Test restoring representative courses in a separate environment, especially when plugins, files and user data differ between source and destination.

name: PDF Protect
description: Display PDFs through a controlled Moodle viewer that removes common download, print and text-copy paths to discourage casual redistribution.
description_html:
Controlled PDF viewingPDF.js viewer

PDF Protect

Publish a PDF as a Moodle activity when you want learners to read it in the browser without presenting the usual download, print and text-copy controls.

The activity uses a customized PDF.js-based viewer and Moodle file access instead of exposing the document through the browser's normal PDF interface.

Reduced casual extraction
  • Hides the standard download controls.
  • Suppresses the viewer's print controls.
  • Restricts normal text-selection/copy interaction.
  • Keeps the resource inside a Moodle activity context.
Custom viewer
Learners interact with the plugin's PDF.js presentation instead of the browser's native PDF toolbar.
Moodle file access
The document is served through Moodle's file handling and activity permissions rather than as an unrelated public file URL.
Simple authoring
Teachers add the PDF as a course activity and learners open it directly in the controlled viewer.
This is deterrence, not absolute DRM. Any document that can be rendered on a user's device can still be captured by determined users through screenshots, browser tooling or other methods. The plugin reduces common and accidental redistribution paths; it cannot make copying technically impossible.
How it fits real Moodle workflows

PDF Protect is designed for controlled access to learning documents inside Moodle. Administrators and teachers need to consider the whole path from the enrolled learner to the displayed or downloaded file, including course permissions and the limits of browser-based document protection. A protected presentation can discourage casual redistribution but cannot guarantee that a person who can see a page is unable to capture it. Use it alongside institutional policies and Moodle access controls instead of promising perfect copy prevention.

name: SuperVideo Filter Player
description: Automatically convert supported video links in Moodle text content into the Super Video player without requiring manual embed code.
description_html:
Media playerSuper Video

SuperVideo Filter Player

Use the Super Video playback experience inside normal Moodle text content, not only inside a dedicated video activity.

When a compatible link is rendered, the media plugin transforms it into the integrated Super Video player automatically.

Best fit
  • Pages, labels, books and editor-driven content.
  • Authors who prefer links over copied iframe/embed HTML.
  • Sites already using mod_supervideo as the video integration layer.
Dependency: the media plugin relies on the Super Video activity/integration being installed and configured.
Features in practice

SuperVideo Filter Player recognizes supported video links embedded in Moodle's regular text areas and turns them into the corresponding SuperVideo playback presentation. Authors can work through their familiar Moodle editor and paste a supported media reference instead of writing their own iframe or player script. When that content is displayed through the configured filter, the embedded experience is generated consistently across resources and course pages. This reduces repeated HTML editing, especially where many teachers create and maintain course content. The separate SuperVideo module must be installed and configured for the player integration to work; the filter does not convert arbitrary unsupported links.

How it fits real Moodle workflows

Filters are most useful when content authors should not have to remember how to configure a player for each new page. Once enabled, the media reference remains part of normal Moodle text, so the same authoring workflow can be reused across many activities. Administrators should test unsupported URLs, edited content and compatibility with the required playback module before turning the filter on site-wide.

name: OttFlix Repository
description: Browse and select OttFlix media from Moodle's repository picker instead of manually copying media references between systems.
description_html:
Moodle repositoryOttFlix library

OttFlix Repository

Bring the OttFlix library into Moodle's normal file-selection workflow so course authors can find media without leaving the editor to copy identifiers or URLs by hand.

Its job is selection and insertion. Playback remains the responsibility of the compatible Moodle media integration, keeping library browsing and rendering as separate concerns.

Author workflow
  1. Open Moodle's repository/file picker.
  2. Browse the available OttFlix media.
  3. Select the desired item.
  4. Insert its reference into the Moodle content being edited.
  5. Let the media layer render the compatible player.
No duplicate media catalog
OttFlix remains the media library; Moodle receives the selected reference through its repository workflow.
Editor-friendly
Teachers use the same repository picker they already know instead of switching applications every time they need a video.
Separation of responsibilities
The repository finds content; the media plugin handles how that content is embedded and played.
How it fits real Moodle workflows

The OttFlix repository plugin brings external media selection into Moodle's familiar file-picker workflow. Instead of asking a teacher to copy opaque references from another system and paste them into a field, it provides a selection interface where supported media can be located and attached in context. Administrators should configure the service connection and verify which users can browse or select remote assets. External availability and access policies remain relevant even after a media reference appears in a Moodle course.

name: OttFlix Filter Player
description: Recognize OttFlix media references in Moodle content and render them with the OttFlix playback integration automatically.
description_html:
Media playerAutomatic embed

OttFlix Filter Player

Turn compatible OttFlix media references in Moodle content into the appropriate embedded player instead of leaving learners with a raw link.

This plugin is the rendering half of the integration: course authors can insert OttFlix content in Moodle, while the media layer recognizes that content and produces the player at display time.

Where it fits
  • OttFlix stores and manages the media.
  • The repository plugin helps authors select it.
  • The media plugin converts the reference into playback.
  • Moodle content keeps the normal editor and display workflow.
Automatic rendering
Compatible references are transformed when Moodle renders the content, reducing manual embed-code handling.
Reusable across content
The media layer can be used wherever Moodle's normal content rendering supports the configured media player.
Library stays external
The integration renders OttFlix media without turning Moodle into a second copy of the OttFlix library.
How it fits real Moodle workflows

The filter is useful when course text should display supported OttFlix references as playable media rather than as unhelpful raw links. Authors continue using familiar Moodle editors, while playback presentation is handled consistently when the content is rendered. This makes it easier to maintain pages that contain many media references without editing iframe code. The integration still depends on supported source formats and a working OttFlix configuration; it does not turn arbitrary third-party URLs into accessible media.

name: Helpdesk and Knowledge Base
description: Integrated ticketing and knowledge base with category teams, scheduled workflows, Kopere BI reporting and AI Bridge-assisted drafting.
description_html:
Service deskKnowledge base

Kopere Helpdesk

Bring support requests into Moodle so the ticket, user, course context, conversation and operational history stay in the same environment.

Users can open and follow tickets while support teams organize work by category, status and priority, add attachments, search conversations and keep reusable answers in the built-in knowledge base.

Operational workflow
  • Category-based support teams and routing.
  • Email notifications for new tickets and replies.
  • Ticket history for status, priority and category changes.
  • Scheduled reminders for unanswered requests.
  • Automatic closing of resolved tickets after the workflow period.
Kopere Dashboard
local_kopere_dashboard provides the administrative foundation used by the plugin.
Kopere BI
local_kopere_bi provides the reporting layer for ticket demand, categories, service time and support activity.
AI-assisted features
AI-assisted features also require AI Bridge.
Built for support teams, not only ticket storage

The Helpdesk combines ticket management, knowledge reuse, reporting and scheduled follow-up so pending work can be identified and acted on instead of disappearing into email threads or external systems.

How it fits real Moodle workflows

A support desk needs more than a ticket form: staff need to see who owns a request, what happened previously, which replies were sent and which issues still need attention. Helpdesk keeps that workflow close to the user's Moodle account and course context, while the knowledge base helps teams reuse answers to common problems. Reminders and reports can help identify bottlenecks, but departments should establish clear ownership and response expectations. AI-assisted drafting, where enabled, remains subject to human review and its separately stated dependency.

name: EadFlix
description: A dark, streaming-inspired Moodle theme with a custom content-discovery frontpage, accessibility tools, course cards and a media-focused visual identity.
description_html:
Streaming-inspiredDark visual identity

EadFlix

Present Moodle more like a content catalog, using a dark visual language and frontpage sections that make courses feel discoverable instead of merely listed.

EadFlix combines a custom frontpage, course presentation changes, accessibility controls, a popup profile experience and configurable footer areas while retaining Moodle as the underlying LMS.

Streaming-style discovery
  • Custom homepage with slideshow, banner and content-list blocks.
  • Dark styling designed for a media-oriented catalog experience.
  • Course activities can be presented as richer visual blocks.
  • Popup-style learner profile and configurable footer areas.
Accessibility controls
Includes tools for contrast, text sizing, spacing, link/heading emphasis and other assisted-reading adjustments, with VLibras integration for Brazilian Portuguese environments.
Course discovery
Frontpage content blocks are designed to surface courses and highlights visually rather than relying only on Moodle's default lists.
Media-first identity
The dark presentation and catalog-style layout make the theme particularly suited to sites where video and visual course covers are central to navigation.
How it fits real Moodle workflows

EadFlix uses a media-oriented visual style to make course discovery feel closer to a streaming catalog, while actual courses and activities remain Moodle resources. A home page with clear course cards and featured content may improve discovery for learners who browse a large catalog. Administrators should verify how navigation works when courses have long names, different cover assets or limited visibility. The dark presentation is an interface choice, not an automatic video platform or replacement for course enrolment rules.

name: Ead Training
description: A training-oriented Moodle theme with accessibility tools, an editable institutional frontpage, course-card presentation and a customizable learner interface.
description_html:
Training portalAccessible customization

Ead Training

Build a branded Moodle training portal with an editable frontpage and stronger course presentation while keeping the interface suitable for academic and corporate learning environments.

Ead Training provides frontpage editing, course-card presentation, accessibility controls, a popup profile interface and configurable footer content without forcing a streaming-style dark identity.

Training-site building blocks
  • Editable homepage with slideshow, banners, resource lists and highlights.
  • Course-page presentation with optional information banners.
  • Activity-card behavior for more visual learning paths.
  • Popup learner profile and configurable footer blocks.
Accessibility toolkit
Supports text sizing, contrast, spacing, navigation assistance and related accessibility adjustments, including VLibras integration for Brazilian Portuguese use.
Editable frontpage
Administrators can compose a more institutional landing page instead of depending exclusively on Moodle's default site-home layout.
Training-first presentation
The visual direction is suited to branded academies and corporate training portals where structure and accessibility matter more than a media-streaming aesthetic.
How it fits real Moodle workflows

Ead Training targets institutional training sites that need a branded entry point, course-card presentation and accessibility controls without rebuilding Moodle activities. Administrators can arrange the front page around the institution's training offering, while teachers retain familiar editing and assessment tools. A useful acceptance test is whether learners can find the right course, recognize their progress and navigate from phone or desktop without unnecessary detours. Theme configuration should be reviewed with real content and keyboard access.

name: System Status
description: Publish a Moodle status page with uptime history, consecutive online days and scheduled availability checks for operational transparency.
description_html:
Availability monitoringPublic status page

System Status

Turn periodic Moodle availability checks into a status page that can be shared with support teams and users.

The plugin records check history, tracks uptime and consecutive online days, and exposes a public read-only status view.

Operational view
  • Current availability state.
  • Check and downtime history.
  • Consecutive days online.
  • Public status URL for communication during incidents.
CRON frequency matters. Moodle CRON must run at least as often as the configured check interval; otherwise missed task windows can look like availability failures.
Features in practice

System Status gives an institution a public availability page supported by scheduled Moodle checks. It shows uptime history and consecutive days reported online, offering context beyond a one-time availability message. Administrators configure how frequently the system should be checked, then share the page with users or support staff who need a basic operational overview. The accuracy of that history depends on Moodle cron: a schedule running less often than the required check interval misses observation windows. Server time, proxy behavior and the selected monitored endpoint should also be checked. The status page reports observed availability rather than guaranteeing every subsystem is healthy.

How it fits real Moodle workflows

For a reliable status history, align the configured check interval with Moodle cron and make sure the observed endpoint really represents the intended service. A public page can reduce repeated support questions during incidents, but it should not expose administrative diagnostics or private monitoring details. Uptime records also need contextual interpretation when scheduled maintenance or a reverse proxy affects the checks.

name: Slow Queries
description: Turn existing Moodle query logs into an admin interface for finding slow SQL, recurring bottlenecks, callers and CRON-versus-WEB performance problems.
description_html:
Database performanceAdmin-only

Slow Queries

Turn a table full of query timings into something an administrator can actually use to answer: which SQL is slow, how often does it happen, and where is it coming from?

The plugin reads an existing {log_queries} data source and provides filtering, triage and context for Moodle database performance investigations.

From symptom to caller
  • Filter by execution time and query metadata.
  • Separate CRON-originated queries from web requests.
  • Derive a practical caller from the captured backtrace.
  • Inspect SQL, parameters, errors and timing together.
  • Look for recurrence instead of chasing one isolated spike.
Performance triage
Start with the worst execution times, then narrow the problem by caller, request type and recurrence before touching indexes or application code.
Backtrace context
The UI skips the generic Moodle DML frames and surfaces the next meaningful frame, which is usually much closer to the component that triggered the database call.
Best-effort SQL reconstruction
Common parameter formats are parsed so positional values can be shown with the statement for investigation, while making no claim that every logger format can be reconstructed perfectly.
This is a viewer, not a query collector. The environment must already record query data in {log_queries}. Access is intentionally restricted because SQL, parameters and backtraces may contain sensitive operational information.

name: Kopere Email
description: Replace Moodle's default email output with branded wrappers, provider-specific templates, placeholders, import/export and digest handling for group conversations.
description_html:
Message outputBranded email

Kopere Email

Keep Moodle's notification system while gaining control over the final email layout and over the content sent by selected message providers.

A global HTML wrapper standardizes visual identity, while provider-specific templates can replace subject/body content for notifications that need a more deliberate communication experience.

Email customization layer
  • Global HTML wrapper with header/footer branding.
  • Custom subject and HTML per Moodle message provider.
  • Mustache-style placeholders for site, recipient, sender, course and message data.
  • Import/export for wrappers and custom provider templates.
  • Digest queue for group-conversation messages.
Migration-aware: installation migrates relevant email-processor settings so sites do not accidentally send both the default Moodle email and the customized Kopere Email copy.
Features in practice

Kopere Email lets site administrators apply institutional branding and tailored HTML templates through Moodle's email message-output workflow, without altering each notification producer. A reusable wrapper can provide a common header, footer and styling, while particular providers can use event-specific templates and placeholders. Messages still need useful plain-text representations for email clients that prefer them. Import and export support moving template sets between installations and test environments. Because email output can affect a large range of system notifications, administrators should check provider routing, generated links, placeholder substitution and rendering before changing a production configuration.

How it fits real Moodle workflows

Template maintenance should be part of release management: verify messages when a Moodle plugin introduces new message providers, and test import/export on a staging site before copying templates to production. The HTML wrapper controls visual consistency, but the plain-text body must remain understandable for accessibility and clients that do not render HTML. Provider-specific substitutions need to preserve intended recipients and links.

name: Child Course
description: Link a parent course to a child course with optional automatic enrolment, group inheritance, completion rules and incremental grade/completion synchronization.
description_html:
Course compositionEnrolment and sync

Child Course

Represent another Moodle course as an activity inside the current course and optionally automate the access relationship between the two.

The activity can enrol learners into the child course, manage group relationships and use child-course progress as part of the parent-course completion experience.

Cross-course workflow
  • Redirect learners from the activity to the child course.
  • Optional automatic enrolment and role preservation.
  • Specific-group assignment or inherited parent groups.
  • Completion based on child-course completion or tracked activities.
  • Incremental grade/completion synchronization with manual sync option.
  • Backup/restore and Moodle App access support.
Features in practice

Child Course lets a parent course link to another existing Moodle course, optionally enrolling the learner and synchronizing selected learning results back to the parent. It is useful when several learning paths share one common course and duplication would make content maintenance difficult. Teachers configure the target, enrolment behavior, optional groups and roles, as well as completion or grade synchronization rules. The learner opens the activity and is redirected to the child course instead of a copied module. If automatic enrolment is disabled, existing permission requirements still apply. Institutions should also decide what happens to enrolments when the link is removed.

How it fits real Moodle workflows

Shared child courses reduce duplicated maintenance, but completion and grade synchronization require clear semantics. Define which activities count, which enrolment context owns the learner and how group relationships should transfer. Test the behavior when a user has already completed the shared course or does not have permission to access it. Those edge cases matter more than merely displaying a shortcut.

name: Scientific Calculator
description: Provide a client-side scientific calculator activity with trigonometry, logarithms, powers, factorials, history and a parser that does not use eval().
description_html:
Scientific calculatorClient-side

Scientific Calculator

Give learners a course activity for common scientific calculations without sending entered expressions to an external service.

The calculator includes arithmetic, powers, roots, trigonometric and inverse-trigonometric functions, logarithms, rounding helpers, constants and factorials.

Safer expression handling

Expressions are tokenized, converted with a shunting-yard parser and evaluated from RPN instead of being passed to JavaScript eval().

A local on-page history lets learners reuse previous results without creating a stored personal calculation history in Moodle.
Features in practice

Scientific Calculator provides a responsive calculation interface inside a Moodle activity, supporting arithmetic, mathematical constants, powers, roots, trigonometry, logarithms and factorials. Learners can type an expression and use the on-page history to revisit earlier results while solving exercises. Teachers may place the tool beside science or mathematics lessons so students can check intermediate calculations without navigating away from the course. Expressions are interpreted by a dedicated parser rather than JavaScript eval, reducing the risk of executing entered code. The calculator computes values; it does not grade explanations or keep a personal database of student calculations.

How it fits real Moodle workflows

A client-side parser is a useful design choice for a calculator because an input expression should be treated as a mathematical statement, not arbitrary executable JavaScript. The activity can support numerical work without recording each student's intermediate values. Teachers can pair it with questions that require explanation, ensuring learners do not confuse obtaining a numeric result with demonstrating the method.

name: Public Sitemap
description: Generate a standards-compliant XML sitemap from public Moodle content while respecting visibility and guest-access rules.
description_html:
Public discoveryXML sitemap

Public Sitemap

Expose Moodle's public content through a valid XML sitemap so crawlers can discover the pages that are actually intended to be public.

The sitemap is generated from Moodle data instead of a manually maintained URL list, and the plugin respects visibility when deciding what can be exposed.

Public content sources
  • Site front page.
  • Visible course categories.
  • Visible courses eligible for public discovery.
  • Public Moodle blog entries.
  • Forums available in public or guest-accessible contexts.
  • Visible activities placed on the front page.
Dynamic XML
Generates absolute URLs and ISO-8601 modification dates using Moodle data at request time.
Automatic discovery hint
Adds a sitemap reference to the page head so compatible crawlers and SEO tools can detect the endpoint.
Visibility first
Hidden categories, hidden activities and content that should not be public are not treated as indexable pages.
A sitemap improves discovery, not ranking. The plugin helps search engines find public Moodle URLs; it does not promise higher search positions.
How it fits real Moodle workflows

Public Sitemap helps search engines and visitors discover pages that are actually intended to be public. Institutions should distinguish visible catalog content from course material protected by enrolment, because putting private links in a sitemap does not make them suitable for indexing. Administrators should review the generated URLs after changes to course visibility, navigation or the site's base address. A useful sitemap reflects the public information architecture, not every internal object stored in Moodle.

name: Kopere WP Bridge
description: Synchronize completed WooCommerce orders with Moodle course enrolments and cohorts using mapped products, signed webhooks and scheduled reconciliation.
description_html:
WooCommerceMoodle enrolment

Kopere WP Bridge

Turn WooCommerce purchases into Moodle access without maintaining a second enrolment workflow by hand.

Products can be mapped to courses and cohorts; when an order completes, the bridge identifies the customer, creates the Moodle account when necessary and applies the mapped access.

Order-to-access flow
  1. Map a WooCommerce product to one or more Moodle destinations.
  2. Receive the completed-order webhook.
  3. Validate the local token and WooCommerce HMAC signature.
  4. Resolve or create the Moodle user.
  5. Enrol in mapped courses and add to mapped cohorts.
  6. Record processing so reconciliation can safely retry pending items.
Product mappings
One commercial product can drive course enrolment, cohort membership or both, keeping catalog logic outside Moodle course administration.
Webhook validation
Incoming order events are checked using a local endpoint token and WooCommerce signature validation before access is processed.
Scheduled reconciliation
A scheduled task revisits recent completed sales so transient webhook failures do not silently become missing enrolments.
Designed for idempotent commerce workflows

The bridge treats the webhook as the fast path and scheduled synchronization as the safety net, which is much more reliable than assuming every external callback will arrive exactly once and at the perfect moment.

How it fits real Moodle workflows

Kopere WP Bridge connects Moodle-related workflows with a WordPress-facing site, which is common when marketing content and learning delivery live on separate platforms. The integration is valuable when user navigation or commercial enrolment flows need to cross that boundary with a predictable contract. Administrators should make responsibilities explicit: which platform owns identities, course access, payments and error handling. Secure credentials and consistent synchronization matter more than merely making two screens appear visually connected.

name: Kopere Proctoring
description: Policy-based quiz proctoring with explicit student rules, incident evidence, verifiable agreements, focus/fullscreen controls and attempt review.
description_html:
Exam integrityPolicy-based

Kopere Proctoring

Apply the controls an exam actually needs, explain them to the student before the attempt and preserve reviewable evidence when something happens during the assessment.

The plugin is built around independent policies rather than one opaque “proctoring mode”, so institutions can combine controls according to the assessment context.

Current policy families
  • Contract and honesty agreement.
  • Copy, cut, paste, print and context-menu restrictions.
  • Focus and tab/application change monitoring.
  • Fullscreen enforcement.
  • Notifications for relevant exam events.
  • Browser and environment security signals.
Student-visible rules
Mandatory conditions are presented before the exam starts, so monitoring is part of the declared assessment rules rather than hidden behavior.
Incident evidence
Attempt context and policy incidents can be reviewed later with timestamps and relevant environment information instead of relying on a single yes/no flag.
Extensible policies
Policies follow a shared discovery and lifecycle architecture, which keeps individual controls isolated and makes new evidence types possible without rewriting the entire proctoring flow.
Agreement with verifiable evidence

When the contract policy is enabled, the institution can present an honor code, privacy notice or exam rules before access is released. Acceptance can produce a PDF receipt with verification data, creating an auditable record that the learner received and accepted the declared conditions.

Different exams can use different controls

A low-stakes activity may need only an agreement, while a controlled final exam can combine fullscreen, focus, copy restrictions, security signals, notifications and teacher-controlled access. The goal is proportional control, not forcing every quiz into the same restrictive experience.

Signals are evidence, not a verdict. A focus change, fullscreen exit or browser anomaly can have legitimate causes. Kopere Proctoring records context for review and does not treat one incident as automatic proof of misconduct.

name: Video Progress
description: Track the video segments students actually watch, with completion, grades, timelines, analytics and synchronized learning interactions. Requires Video Bridge.
description_html:
Also requires Video Bridge.

Track what was actually watched

Video Progress turns video into a complete Moodle activity with progress based on the segments the learner really watched. Moving the playhead to the end does not produce 100% completion: skipped regions remain unwatched, while repeated regions increase playback time without artificially increasing the unique-content percentage.

The activity integrates completion, grades, reports and timelines so teachers can distinguish the last watched position, unique content watched, total playback time, repeated segments and audience drop-off points.

Video sources and learning resources

Video sources are extensible through subplugins and currently include uploads, direct URLs, YouTube and Vimeo. Activities can also include captions, Bloom-based learning objectives, support materials and synchronized content displayed at specific moments in the video.

  • Segment-based viewing progress and playback resume.
  • Completion rules based on a minimum percentage actually watched.
  • Gradebook integration using the watched percentage.
  • Individual and aggregated class timelines.
  • Most-watched, least-watched and audience drop-off analysis.
  • Optional forward-seeking restrictions and playback-speed limits.
  • WebVTT and SRT captions.
  • Bloom learning objectives and complementary materials.
  • Synchronized notes and mandatory quiz interactions during playback.
  • CSV export, progress reset, backup and restore, Privacy API and Moodle app integration.
Extensible architecture

Sources, objectives, materials and synchronized content are implemented through dedicated subplugin types, allowing new formats and video platforms to be added without changing the activity core.

name: Recertification
description: Run auditable recertification cycles that archive selected learner history before resetting progress, with simulation, scheduling and rollback-safe execution.
description_html:
RecertificationAudit-first reset

Kopere Recertification

Repeat a certification cycle without pretending the learner's previous cycle never existed.

Before selected progress is reset, the engine builds an execution plan, preserves configured history and files, validates the preservation phase and only then performs cleanup.

Archive first, reset second
  1. Build the plan in real course order.
  2. Create enabled history snapshots.
  3. Validate and copy enabled file archives through Moodle File API.
  4. Clean selected activity and system data only after preservation succeeds.
  5. Commit the cycle, then emit business events and notifications.
Transactional safety
Each user/course execution uses a Moodle lock and delegated transaction so a preservation or cleanup failure does not accept a partially reset cycle.
Real simulation
Simulation runs the same providers and selection logic inside a transaction that is always rolled back, including file-source validation without permanent file-pool side effects.
Auditable cycles
History, copied files, logs and notification records remain tied to the recertification cycle so the previous state can be reviewed later.
Scheduling that reflects certification reality

Course policies can reference enrolment, fixed annual dates, course completion, a certificate/reference provider or the last completed recertification cycle. Automatic cycles are queued per user, while administrative and bulk workflows remain independent so one failure does not poison an entire batch.

Before the due date
Scheduled state supports warning notifications without prematurely declaring the current certification invalid.
At the due date
The cycle becomes pending and is processed through an independent ad-hoc task for the learner.
Extensible data providers

Specialized recerttask_* providers isolate component-specific history and cleanup rules. The current package includes providers for quiz, forum, grades, activity completion, course completion, competency and enrolment, plus integrations such as Certificate Beautiful, Child Course, Super Video and Video Progress.

Generic cleanup is deliberately conservative: it is limited to eligible activity tables and approved user-bound conditions rather than guessing which records are safe to delete.

Recertification is not a blind reset button. The design intentionally makes preservation, validation, simulation and auditability part of the operation before destructive processing is accepted.

name: H5Prime Viewer
description: Use H5Prime as Moodle's H5P rendering layer while keeping content, metadata and saved state in Moodle's native H5P subsystem.
description_html:
H5P runtimeH5Prime

H5Prime Viewer

Replace the H5P presentation layer without inventing another activity, another content format or another content repository.

h5plib_vh5prime plugs into Moodle's H5P library-handler architecture and renders existing H5P content through the H5Prime runtime.

What stays in Moodle
  • H5P content and metadata.
  • Language and user context.
  • Saved user state supplied by Moodle.
  • Existing H5P workflows and content management.
Native handler integration
Registers H5Prime where Moodle expects an H5P library handler instead of patching core rendering code.
Bundled runtime assets
Ships the JavaScript, styles, templates and translations needed by the H5Prime viewer as part of the Moodle plugin.
No external account
Rendering does not depend on creating a separate hosted-service account just to display the H5P content already stored in Moodle.
A viewer, not a parallel H5P platform

The distinction matters: teachers continue creating and managing H5P through Moodle, while H5Prime is responsible for how compatible content is presented at runtime. That keeps ownership and lifecycle in Moodle and makes the rendering layer replaceable.

How it fits real Moodle workflows

H5Prime Viewer is useful when institutions have H5P content that should be delivered through a dedicated viewer experience. Authors and administrators need to check the content libraries and versions used by the existing activities rather than assuming that any interactive package behaves identically after a change in presentation. Test representative exercises, embedded media, mobile layouts and completion behavior if the surrounding course depends on the result. The viewer should preserve the authored educational interaction instead of requiring content to be recreated.

name: Missing Students
description: Identify inactive learners by course and review retention indicators, risk distribution, absence ranges and CSV exports.
description_html:
Missing Students

Identify learners who have been inactive for a meaningful period and turn course-access data into a practical retention dashboard.

Focus on learners who should actually be monitored

Missing Students works at course level and uses Moodle's completion-report population rules so the report focuses on participants who are relevant to course monitoring instead of treating every enrolled account as an equal retention case.

The inactivity threshold is configurable. The report distinguishes time since the learner last accessed the current course from the learner's last access to Moodle as a whole, giving teachers a clearer picture of whether the problem is course-specific or broader.

Retention dashboard
  • Course-access inactivity based on the learner's latest access to the current course.
  • Site-access inactivity based on the learner's latest Moodle access.
  • Indicators and risk distribution for quickly identifying the most urgent cases.
  • Absence ranges and a criticality ranking to support follow-up prioritization.
  • Filters that help teachers narrow the report to the learners who need attention.
  • CSV export for contact workflows, external analysis or institutional retention processes.
From data to follow-up

The plugin is intended to make inactivity actionable. Instead of presenting raw access logs, it organizes the information into a course-oriented view that can support outreach, tutoring, retention campaigns and other learner-support routines.

How it fits real Moodle workflows

Missing Students turns inactivity information into an operational starting point for learner follow-up. Staff can compare courses, review absence ranges and filter participants who have not returned recently, while exports support work outside the dashboard when authorized. The most useful workflow is to investigate the context behind an inactivity signal before contacting a student: enrolment dates, course schedules and expected activity can change its meaning. Low activity is not, by itself, proof that someone has abandoned a course.

name: Private Notes
description: Give each learner a private per-user note area inside a course activity without exposing notes to other users.
description_html:
Private Notes

Give every learner a private writing space inside a Moodle course without exposing note content to classmates or teachers.

A private note attached to the learning context

Teachers can place a Private Notes activity next to a video, page, lesson or any other course content. Each learner opens the activity and writes with Moodle's standard editor, creating one personal note area for that activity.

The note belongs to the current authenticated user. The content API does not accept an arbitrary user id, so a learner cannot request another learner's note by changing a URL or request parameter.

Privacy by design
  • One private note per learner and activity.
  • Other learners never see the note.
  • Teachers do not receive a capability that exposes note text.
  • Optional teacher metadata can be disabled, aggregated only, or limited to learner identity and created/modified dates.
  • Individual teacher metadata deliberately excludes the note content itself.
  • No external service or client-side dependency is required.
Useful alongside course content

Private Notes is suitable for personal reflections, study reminders, observations while watching a lesson, preparation notes and other learner-owned writing that should stay inside Moodle without becoming a submission or discussion.

How it fits real Moodle workflows

Private Notes supports an individual learner workspace for keeping course reflections and observations without publishing them to classmates. It is useful for ongoing study journals where learners need somewhere to write between formal assignments, and where a teacher may have a defined review role. The access model should be clear from the activity settings so participants understand who can read their notes. A private learning note is not the same as a forum post or a graded submission.

name: Branching Video
description: Create interactive branching videos with decisions, alternate paths, multiple endings, resume and learner path tracking.
description_html:
Branching Video

Create interactive videos in which learner decisions change what happens next, allowing alternate paths, reconnection points and multiple endings.

Decisions inside the video

Teachers add one or more videos and place decisions at specific timecodes. Each answer option can send the learner to another point in the same video, to another video, to another decision or directly to a named ending.

Paths do not need to remain permanently separate. Different branches can reconnect later, making it possible to model realistic scenarios without duplicating every scene.

Learning path tracking
  • Uploaded video, direct media URL, YouTube and Vimeo sources.
  • Decision history recorded for each learner.
  • Resume support for unfinished branching paths.
  • Teacher control over whether earlier choices may be changed.
  • Optional display of the completed path after the learner reaches an ending.
  • Completion can be tied to reaching a valid ending.
Reports for scenario analysis

Teacher reports show decision histories, option distribution, commonly used paths, abandonment points and reached endings. This makes the activity useful for simulations, case-based learning, consequence-driven training and other situations where the route taken is as important as the final destination.

How it fits real Moodle workflows

Branching Video lets a teacher design alternative viewing paths, turning decisions at selected moments into different sequences of content. It works best when each choice has a meaningful pedagogical consequence rather than merely sending a learner to the next clip. Before publishing, teachers should test all routes, confirm that learners can understand the available options and review what happens when a branch cannot be reached. Completion or reporting should represent the actual route followed rather than assuming everyone watched identical material.

name: GeniAI Chat
description: Add a course activity that exposes the GeniAI chat experience inside Moodle.
description_html:
GeniAI Chat

Place the GeniAI conversational experience directly inside a Moodle course as a standard course activity.

Course-level access to GeniAI

GeniAI Chat acts as the course activity layer for the local GeniAI service. Learners open the activity from the course and receive the configured GeniAI chat interface without leaving Moodle.

The activity passes the current course context to the GeniAI chat experience, allowing the conversation entry point to be presented as part of the normal course flow rather than as a separate site-wide tool.

Uses the shared GeniAI configuration
  • Uses the GeniAI name and operating mode configured by the local GeniAI plugin.
  • Shows the course-aware introductory messaging supplied by GeniAI.
  • Respects Moodle course login and the activity view capability.
  • Exposes management controls only to users who hold the GeniAI management capability.
  • Uses Moodle's standard activity-view event and completion-by-view behavior.
  • The activity module itself does not declare plugin-specific personal-data storage.
A simple activity wrapper

The module intentionally keeps its own settings small: the course activity provides the name, description and normal Moodle activity settings, while the conversational behavior is supplied by the installed local GeniAI plugin. This avoids duplicating provider and chat configuration inside every course activity.

How it fits real Moodle workflows

GeniAI Chat turns conversational assistance into a Moodle activity so teachers can establish a context and guide how learners interact with an assistant. An activity-specific chat is easier to relate to course objectives than an unrestricted external chatbot, but the distinction between generated guidance and authoritative teaching material must remain visible. Teachers should test prompts, review permissions and decide how students are expected to verify model answers. Availability, costs and privacy constraints depend on the configured AI infrastructure and site policies.

name: Phrase Wall
description: Collect one short phrase from each learner and display the responses in a visual wall, optionally anonymously.
description_html:
Phrase Wall

Collect one concise contribution from each learner and display the class responses as a visual wall.

Short responses instead of long discussions

Phrase Wall is designed for reflections, summaries, takeaways, opinions, exit prompts and other activities where the teacher wants one focused sentence from each participant instead of a forum thread or long-form submission.

The teacher defines the maximum sentence length and whether learner names should be visible to participants. Each learner submits one phrase and the wall presents the class responses according to those settings.

Main features
  • One sentence per learner.
  • Configurable sentence limit from 60 to 280 characters.
  • Identified or anonymous participant-facing wall.
  • Optional editing of the learner's own sentence.
  • Teacher report that retains authorship even when the wall is anonymous.
  • Teacher ability to delete submissions.
  • Optional activity completion after submission.
  • Responsive interface for desktop and mobile use.
Simple learner and teacher workflows

Learners open the activity, write within the configured limit and submit. Teachers get a compact overview of participation without turning the activity into a conversation stream, while still retaining the management information required for moderation and follow-up.

How it fits real Moodle workflows

Phrase Wall makes short contributions visible as a shared learning artifact, useful for brainstorming, defining a concept or collecting concise answers from a class. Teachers can pose a prompt and then discuss patterns that emerge in students' responses instead of reading a long essay from each participant. Clear participation instructions matter: whether classmates can view submissions and how contributions are moderated should match the course's needs. A short phrase can start discussion but rarely provides enough evidence for a complete assessment.

name: AJAX Chat
description: Provide real-time course chat with text, recorded audio, attachments, reactions, polls and lightweight file-backed polling.
description_html:
AJAX Chat

Provide a live course chat with text, recorded audio, attachments, reactions and teacher-managed polls while keeping frequent read polling away from normal database-heavy page requests.

Real-time conversation inside the course

Learners can exchange text messages, record audio in supported browsers and attach files when those options are enabled. Users can react to messages and may edit or delete their own message during the first 60 seconds after sending it.

Teacher controls for live sessions
  • Enable or disable the chat when the conversation should be opened or paused.
  • Delete messages when moderation is required.
  • Block and unblock participants.
  • Create polls that remain pinned at the top or in a side panel until they are closed.
  • Set an availability date before which learners cannot read the history or use the composer.
Lightweight polling architecture

The chat maintains its frequently read state in files under the protected Moodle data area, including recent-message indexes and a lightweight event stream. This allows history and polling requests to read the chat state without repeatedly performing normal plugin SELECT queries on every browser poll.

Protected attachment delivery

Stored attachments remain outside the public web root and are served through opaque file identifiers. Active-content file types such as HTML, JavaScript and SVG are rejected, while non-media files are delivered as downloads.

name: Class Check-in
description: Register class attendance inside a configurable time window with optional code, IP and geolocation restrictions.
description_html:
Class Check-in

Register attendance during a controlled time window with optional code, network and geolocation checks.

A direct attendance workflow

The learner opens the activity during the configured window and uses the check-in action to register presence. Teachers can keep the process simple or add additional checks when the class context requires them.

A numeric code can be required and regenerated by the teacher. The activity can also compare the learner's detected public IP address with the reference IP captured by the teacher, or verify that the learner is within a configured geographic radius of a teacher-captured location.

Attendance controls and reporting
  • Configurable opening and closing window.
  • Optional 4- or 6-digit attendance code.
  • Optional same-public-IP validation against the teacher reference.
  • Optional browser geolocation validation within a configurable radius.
  • Report showing present and pending/absent learners.
  • Registration time, IP and location information when those checks are enabled.
  • Activity completion after a successful check-in.
Designed with realistic presence signals

IP matching is useful when the class shares the same network and public NAT address, but it is treated as a network signal rather than cryptographic proof of physical presence. Geolocation similarly depends on the position and accuracy reported by the learner's browser.

How it fits real Moodle workflows

Class Check-in records attendance or presence within a teacher-defined window, with optional additional constraints such as an access code, IP range or geolocation. This can reduce manual register handling for scheduled meetings, but it is important to configure the timing and location rules for the actual learning environment. A mobile learner behind carrier NAT or an institution behind a proxy may not match simplistic network assumptions. Teachers should review exceptions and retain a process for correcting attendance records when legitimate participants cannot check in.

name: Link Collection
